source_text: Verum hactenus mitiore sim functus eloquio, nunc autem splendor flammeae rationis ostendit malis et bonis, profanis et sacris, piis et impiis, iustis et iniquis nullum esse consortium atque ideo inter praecepta et iudicia Dei nihil esse pugnarum, contrarium autem esse aliena peccata aliis imputare et, eadem ne imputentur, iubere, quoniam de his duobus necesse est uno concesso alterum summoveri, id est uno iusto alterum iniquum doceri, in legem autem Dei praescriptum esse, ne parentum peccata filiis imputentur [n41] , ac per hoc eadem auctoritate contrarium eius id est opinionem traducis cum Manichaeis funditus corruisse.
pass_a_gloss: But thus far I have used milder speech; now however the splendor of flaming reason shows that to evils and goods, profane and sacred, pious and impious, just and unjust there is no partnership, and therefore between the precepts and judgments of God there is nothing of fights, but it is contrary to impute others' sins to others and to command that the same not be imputed, since of these two it is necessary that with one granted the other be removed, that is with one just the other be taught unjust, but in the law of God it has been prescribed that parents' sins not be imputed to sons, and through this by the same authority its contrary, that is the opinion of the vine-layer, has collapsed from the foundation with the Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Enough of gentler speech. The brightness of blazing reason now shows that evil and good, profane and sacred, godly and ungodly, just and unjust have no partnership. Therefore there is no conflict between God’s commands and judgments. Charging people with others’ sins is contrary to commanding that those same sins must not be charged to them. Of these two, accepting one necessarily excludes the other; showing one just shows the other unjust. Yet God’s law prescribes that parents’ sins must not be charged to their children (Deuteronomy 24:16). Consequently, by that same authority, its opposite—the theory of inherited sin—has collapsed completely, together with the Manichaeans.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
